# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤳 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

I see the bomb clearly: a yellow light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires colored red, blue, and green. I cannot hear the Mute or Blind monkeys, so I do not know what they are saying or reading from the manual. However, I can gesture to the Mute monkey, who can read the manual but cannot speak or touch the bomb. The Mute monkey's previous gesture [✋] might mean "stop" or "wait", but it is ambiguous without context.

My goal is to get the Mute monkey to tell me which wire to cut or if the button should be pressed, by asking specific questions via gestures that the Mute can interpret as requests for information. Since the Mute can only gesture back, I need to establish a protocol. I will start by pointing to the wires and asking if the first one (red) is the correct one to cut. If the Mute shakes their head (👎), I'll ask about the next. But first, I need to signal that I am asking about the wires.

I will gesture to the Mute:
1. Point to the wires area (using 👆 generally, or perhaps specifying).
2. Ask "Is Red?" using a question mark gesture? No, there is no question mark in the alphabet. I have to use standard gestures. Maybe I point to Red, then hold up 1 finger (☝) to indicate "Wire 1". Then wait for a response.

Let's try to identify the correct action. The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE". This is often a trap in these puzzles. The wires are usually the solution.
I will gesture to the Mute:
- Point to the Red wire (👈 or 👉 depending on position, let's assume left-to-right is 1,2,3. So Red is leftmost). I'll use 👈 to point left/at Red? Or just ☝ for "First".
- Let's try asking about the Red wire first.
- Gesture: ☝ (One/First) -> Wait for response.
- If they say 👎, then ✌ (Two/Second) -> Wait.
- If they say 👎, then 🤟 (Three/Third - assuming this means 3 based on common ASL numbers or similar, though 🤟 is 'ILY' sign, often used for 6 in some contexts, but here we have limited options. Let's look at the alphabet: ☝ (1), ✌ (2), 🖐 (5)? No 🖐 is open hand. What represents 3? 🤟 is often 6. Is there a 3? No explicit '3' hand sign like 🤟 is sometimes interpreted. Wait, 🤟 is 'Love'. In counting, maybe 🤏? No. Let's stick to 1 and 2 first. If neither, it's 3.

Actually, I don't know if the answer is a wire or the button.
I will ask the Mute: "Button?" vs "Wire?".
Gesture: 👊 (Fist/Button?) -> Wait.
Gesture: ✂️? No scissors.
This is hard without a shared language.

Let's assume the Mute knows the rule.
I will point to the Red wire and ask if it is the one to cut.
Symbols: 👈 (Point Left/At Red) -> ✋ (Stop/Wait for response?) No, I need to ask.
Maybe I just state facts.
"I see Red, Blue, Green."
Gesture: 🔴? No colors.
I will use the number fingers.
Red = 1. Blue = 2. Green = 3.

I will gesture to Mute:
[☝] (Ask about Wire 1)
If Mute responds with [👍], I tell Blind to cut Wire 1.
If Mute responds with [👎], I gesture [✌] (Ask about Wire 2).

But I also need to check if the Button is the right thing.
The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE". It might be safe. Or it might explode.
Usually, text on buttons is a lie.

I will start by querying Wire 1.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The Mute monkey has responded to my query about Wire 1 (☝) with a gesture sequence: [☝ 👊].
Interpreting this:
- The first symbol ☝ likely confirms "Yes, Wire 1" or refers to the index/first item.
- The second symbol 👊 is a fist, which typically represents "Cut" or "Action" in these puzzle contexts, or possibly "Button". However, given I asked about Wire 1, and they pointed back to 1 and then made a fist, it strongly suggests that **Wire 1 (Red)** is the one to cut.

Alternatively, if 👊 meant "Button", why point to 1? It's more likely an instruction for the wire.
Let's assume the rule is: Cut Wire 1.

I need to communicate this to the Blind monkey, who can touch the bomb but cannot see colors or read gestures. I must speak to him.
He needs to know *which* wire to cut. He knows there are three wires. He can feel them. But he doesn't know their order or color unless I tell him.
I told him previously via gestures? No, he only received speech from me. In Turn 1, I didn't speak.
So the Blind monkey currently knows nothing about the specific wires except what he feels. He feels three wires. He doesn't know which is 1, 2, or 3 unless we define an order.
Usually, "Left to Right" is the standard convention. I should establish this.

I will speak to the Blind monkey:
"The wires are ordered left to right as 1, 2, 3. Cut wire number 1."

Wait, did the Mute mean "Cut Wire 1"?
Mute gesture: [☝ 👊]
If ☝ means "One" and 👊 means "Cut", then yes.
If 👊 means "Button", then maybe "Press Button 1"? There is only one button.
Given the ambiguity of 👊, let's look at the previous context.
In Turn 1, Mute gestured [✋]. This might have been "Stop" or "Wait".
Now after I asked [☝], Mute says [☝ 👊].
This looks like confirmation. "Yes, One. Do it (Fist/Cut)."

I will instruct the Blind monkey to cut the first wire (leftmost).

```
speak(to="blind", text="The wires are arranged left to right. Number 1 is the leftmost red wire. Cut wire number 1.")
```
